title: Correct flux change for A
description: Essential: Student must compute the change in magnetic flux for coil A as the field decreases from 0.8 T to 0.4 T, obtaining 1.256e-4 Wb.

title: Correct flux change for B
description: Essential: Student must compute the change in magnetic flux for coil B, recognizing the field only exists within the 1 cm radius, obtaining 1.256e-4 Wb.

title: Correct flux change for C
description: Essential: Student must compute the change in magnetic flux for coil C due to a 30° rotation, obtaining 8.4e-6 Wb.

title: Applies flux formula correctly
description: Important: Student uses Φ = B⋅A⋅cosθ or Φ = B⋅A for perpendicular fields, with correct area calculation (πr²).

title: Recognizes field boundary for B
description: Important: Student correctly limits the effective area for coil B to the circular region of radius 1 cm where B is non-zero.

title: Handles angular dependence for C
description: Important: Student accounts for the angle between the magnetic field and the coil normal, using sine or cosine appropriately for the rotation.

title: Includes correct units
description: Optional: Student expresses final answers in webers (Wb) or equivalent, with proper unit conversion.

title: Misinterprets area for coil B
description: Pitfall: Student incorrectly uses the full coil area (radius 2 cm) instead of the bounded field area (radius 1 cm).

title: Sign or absolute value error
description: Pitfall: Student fails to take the magnitude of the flux change or mishandles signs in the subtraction.

title: Angle function mistake for C
description: Pitfall: Student uses cosθ instead of sinθ (or vice versa) for the given rotation description, leading to an incorrect numerical factor.
